messages:
Maya CSM: Heads-up: planning a reserved-pool burn-in for AtlasCorp tomorrow 10:00 PDT. Objective: validate quota, autoscaler behavior, and load scripts before their go-live next week.
Tom (AtlasCorp): I'll join. Peak concurrency target: ~120 concurrent requests, avg sequence ~512 tokens, bursts up to 180 QPS.
Rachel SE: Please paste a representative payload and expected QPS distribution so we can confirm model variant and kv-cache settings.
Tom (AtlasCorp): Sample profile: avg request ~550 tokens, daily steady ~1.2k prompts but bursty. Baseline ~20 QPS, ramp to 180 QPS for short bursts (2-3m).
Aj SRE: From infra: confirm whether traffic is sticky to the reserved pool and if fallback is allowed for the window. Also need quota numbers to pre-provision.
Maya CSM: We want sticky routing to the reserved capacity for the whole test; no automatic fallback. Any fallback will be manual.
Liam EngInfra: Proposed autoscaler config to start discussion:
```json
{
  \"min_replicas\": 2,
  \"max_replicas\": 14,
  \"scale_up_threshold_qps_per_gpu\": 22,
  \"scale_down_threshold_qps_per_gpu\": 11,
  \"cooldown_seconds\": 45
}
```
This should hit target concurrency with room for short bursts. Thoughts?
Rachel SE: Suggest enabling prefix KV caching for repeated prompt templates and set batch size cap to 8 to reduce memory pressure. Also ensure tokenization differences are handled in the loadgen.
Tom (AtlasCorp): We'll provide a test API key scoped to the reserved pool. Please don't send any live customer data in logs. I'll upload a sanitized sample prompt set: https://files.atlascorp.example/prompt-set-2026-03
Aj SRE: Run plan for tomorrow (timeline):
- 09:30 provisioning smoke (low qps)
- 09:45 auth/key verification
- 10:00 ramp start (5 stages: 20%, 40%, 70%, 90%, 100%)
- 10:20 2-minute soak at peak
- 10:25 cool down and collect traces/logs
- 10:45 post-run sync and notes
I'll post a quick runbook into #incidents and tag the on-call.
Maya CSM: I'll send invites to Atlas stakeholders and Ops. Tom, please post the test key into the secure ticket before 09:00 tomorrow.
onboard-bot: Calendar event "AtlasCorp reserved pool burn-in" created for 2026-03-22 10:00 PDT. Invitees: Maya CSM, Tom (AtlasCorp), Rachel SE, Aj SRE, Liam EngInfra.
Liam EngInfra: Load script prototype (we'll run k6 for controlled ramps):
```bash
# simplified starter for quick smoke
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do
  curl -s -X POST \"https://inference.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" \\\n    -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY\" \\\n    -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n    -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-7b\",\"input\":\"<sanitized sample>\",\"max_tokens\":512}' &\n  sleep 0.03
done
```
We'll convert into k6 scenarios for ramp shapes.
Rachel SE: Acceptance criteria for the burn-in:
- 95th percentile token latency (streaming) < 400ms
- No OOMs or KV-cache evictions >= 5% during sustained peak
- Autoscaler scales within ramp windows (no stuck replicas)
- Error rate < 0.5% and no request drops
- Successful prefix cache hits >= 20% during soak (if caching enabled)
Aj SRE: I'll monitor autoscaler events, pod restarts, GPU mem usage, and request errors. If error rate rises >0.5% we'll abort to baseline.
Maya CSM: Post-run deliverables: Rachel to prepare a 1-pager on tuning knobs (batching, cache, quantization tradeoffs) and we'll capture perf snapshots for the renewal packet.
Rachel SE: On it. I'll drop the doc in the onboarding folder and do a 10-min walkthrough after the run.
Tom (AtlasCorp): FYI, renewal review in 4 weeks; this run is a gating item for their internal sign-off.
Maya CSM: Noted. We'll prioritize observations and a short summary for the renewal team.
Aj SRE: Quick ask: set reserved-pool quota to 3x expected peak tokens/min to give headroom. I'll verify the quota pre-run.
Tom (AtlasCorp): I requested the quota increase via the portal and got approval from my infra team.
Maya CSM: Perfect. See you all at 09:30 for provisioning. Ping here if anything changes. :thumbsup:
